bereshis.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF (A,S), CHB 2028-10-14 (Chabad 42:5-21). Frankfurt/Posen Ashkenazim also stop at 42:21. Teimani 42:1-16 in EnWP, HeWP and AHT.

noach.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-11-06. Teimani: HeWP and AHT (Rambam's list, Baladi) end at 55:3; Shami Yemenites read 54:1-55:5 (HeWP, AHT). EnWP lists Y with 55:5 and 'some Y' with 55:3.

lech-lecha.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Chabad not listed as differing in SHM.

vayera.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-10-31. Frankfurt/Posen Ashkenazim read 4:1-23 like Sephardim.

chayei-sarah.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Teimani left null: HeWP/EnWP give 1:1-31 (Shami add 1:46); AHT says Yemenite haftara books run to 1:46 and Shami read 1:1-31 then skip to 1:46. Sources conflict.

vayetzei.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF (A,S), CHB 2026-11-21 (via 'Haftorah in a Nutshell' aid 593837 and the text page, Chabad 11:7-12:14). Many Ashkenazim (Chayei Adam; Mishnah Berurah 428:22 per AHT; Vilna/Perushim) add Joel 2:26-27 at the end so as to finish on a positive note; some printed sources (ArtScroll per EnWP) give Sephardim 11:7-13:5. Historically some Ashkenazim read Hosea 11:7-12:12 here.

vayishlach.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-11-28. Minority Ashkenazi custom (some UK congregations; Mishnah Berurah 428 variant per AHT): Hosea 11:7-12:12 instead (the Sephardi Vayetzei haftara).

vayeshev.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Usually displaced by Shabbos Chanukah (Zechariah 2:14-4:7) when Vayeshev falls in Chanukah.

miketz.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Almost always displaced by a Shabbos Chanukah haftara; read only in rare years (EnWP). Teimani from HeWP (all communities) and AHT (no Yemenite variant listed).

shemos.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-01-02. Some Moroccan Sephardim follow the Ashkenazi reading (HeWP, AHT); Baghdad/Libya/Fez/Djerba read Ezekiel 16:1-13 (AHT).

vaera.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Posen began at 29:1.

bo.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Teimani: EnWP and HeWP give Isaiah 19:1-25; AHT says some Yemenites begin at Isaiah 18:7 (Isaiah 18:7-19:25). Several North African communities also read Isaiah 19.

beshalach.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-01-23. Shabbos Shirah.

yisro.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-01-30.

mishpatim.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Usually displaced by Shekalim or Machar Chodesh/Rosh Chodesh Adar (EnWP).

tetzaveh.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Often displaced by Zachor.

ki-sisa.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-02-27. Frankfurt, Worms, Posen Ashkenazim also read 18:20-39. Teimani left null: EnWP gives I Kings 18:1-46, HeWP gives 18:1-45 (AHT lists 18:1-45 for Rambam but does not name Yemen).

vayakhel.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF (S). Rarely read on its own; usually combined with Pekudei or displaced by Shekalim/Parah/HaChodesh. Frankfurt ends at 8:1 (EnWP, AHT). The Ashkenazi Vayakhel text is the same passage that Sephardim read for Pekudei and that everyone reads on the second Shabbos of Chanukah.

pekudei.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-03-13. Posen began at 8:1; Frankfurt read 7:40-8:1 (EnWP, AHT).

tzav.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, CHB 2028-04-08 (Shabbos HaGadol that is not Erev Pesach, so Chabad reads Tzav's own). In most non-leap years Tzav is Shabbos HaGadol; see special.shabbos-hagadol.

shemini.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2028-04-22. Posen also 6:1-19; some Sephardim append 7:16-17 (EnWP).

metzora.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT. Frequently displaced by Shabbos HaGadol (SEF shows Malachi on the dates it sampled).

acharei-mos.notes: Sources: SA OC 428:8 (Rema: Amos 9:7 'Halo kivnei kushiyim' is the haftara of Acharei Mos), EnWP (ArtScroll, Hirsch, Dotan), AHT (Rema, Levush, Aruch HaShulchan, a published Ashkenazi luach, Frankfurt, Posen, Chabad), CHB 2027-05-01 (Chabad Amos). Disputed in Ashkenaz: Hertz, Koren and SEF give Ashkenazim Ezekiel 22:1-19 (or 1-16) for Acharei Mos and Amos for Kedoshim. Because Ezekiel 22 disparages Jerusalem, the Vilna Gaon and R. Soloveitchik read Amos even if it repeats on consecutive weeks (EnWP). Teimani from HeWP (generic) and AHT (most non-Ashkenazi communities, incl. Rambam); EnWP silent.

kedoshim.notes: Sources: EnWP (ArtScroll), AHT (a published Ashkenazi luach, Frankfurt, Posen, Levush), SEF (S), HeWP, CHB 2024-05-11 (Chabad Ezekiel 20:2-20). Disputed in Ashkenaz: Hertz, Koren, SEF etc. give Amos 9:7-15 here (see acharei-mos); Hirsch gives Ezekiel 22:1-19. Teimani Baladi Ezekiel 20:1-15 (HeWP, AHT); Shami begin at 20:1 and run to 20:20 (AHT).

behar.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-05-22 (Chabad 32:6-22). Teimani/Italian read the 'Bechukosai' passage here (EnWP, HeWP).

bechukosai.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Posen read Ezekiel 34:1-15.

bamidbar.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Often displaced by Machar Chodesh (erev Rosh Chodesh Sivan).

nasso.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT (some Baladi Yemenites end at 13:24), SEF.

chukas.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Posen ended earlier (EnWP 11:11, HeWP 11:24: conflicting, not recorded).

pinchas.notes: Own haftara, read only when Pinchas falls before 17 Tammuz (or, in Israel, on it). In most years Pinchas falls after 17 Tammuz and reads the first haftara of affliction, Jeremiah 1:1-2:3 (see special.affliction-1). Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF (dates sampled all after 17 Tammuz). Teimani from HeWP (lists Y) and AHT (common custom, no Yemenite variant); EnWP silent on Y.

matos.notes: Matos is always within the three weeks. When read separately (Pinchas before 17 Tammuz) it carries the first haftara of affliction (special.affliction-1). Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT. Teimani 1:1-19 per EnWP and HeWP; AHT says this was the old Yemenite custom and is still the custom of some Yemenites today.

masei.notes: Second haftara of affliction ('Shim'u'). Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF (A), CHB 2027-07-31 (Chabad, Matos-Masei). Teimani left null: EnWP lists Y with the Sephardi reading and also (citing HeWP) Joshua 1:1-20; HeWP itself gives Isaiah 1:1-20 and notes most Shami follow the Sephardim; AHT says some Baladi Yemenites read Isaiah 1:1-20. Conflicting.

devarim.notes: Shabbos Chazon, third haftara of affliction. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. Teimani 1:21-31 per EnWP and HeWP; AHT notes it is the custom of some Yemenites today (others 1:1-27, or Shami 1:1-20).

vaeschanan.notes: Shabbos Nachamu, first of seven of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-08-14. HeWP notes some read 40:1-27; AHT says 41:17 is added by some Yemenites.

eikev.notes: Second of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF.

reeh.notes: Third of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2025-08-23. When Rosh Chodesh Elul or its eve falls on Shabbos Re'eh the customs differ; see special.shabbos-rosh-chodesh-elul and special.machar-chodesh-elul.

shoftim.notes: Fourth of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF.

ki-seitzei.notes: Fifth of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF. If Re'eh's haftara was displaced by Isaiah 66 (Rosh Chodesh Elul on Shabbos), Ashkenazim and Chabad read Isaiah 54:1-55:5 here (MB 425:7; CHB 2029-08-25); see special.ki-seitzei-after-rosh-chodesh-elul.

ki-savo.notes: Sixth of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF.

nitzavim.notes: Seventh of consolation. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF.

vayelech.notes: Vayelech read on its own always falls between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur, so it takes the Shabbos Shuva haftara (special.shabbos-shuva). When it is joined with Nitzavim, Nitzavim's haftara is read. Sources: AHT, HeWP, EnWP, CHB 2029-09-15 (Chabad Hosea + Micah).

haazinu.notes: Read when Haazinu falls between Yom Kippur and Sukkos (SA OC 428:8). When Haazinu is Shabbos Shuva, the Shabbos Shuva haftara is read instead. Sources: SA OC 428:8, EnWP, HeWP, AHT (most Yemenite communities Ezekiel 17:22-18:32; a few read II Samuel 22), SEF, CHB 2029-09-22.

vezos-haberacha.notes: Read on Simchas Torah, never on an ordinary Shabbos (same as special.simchas-torah). Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, CHB 2026-10-04.

vayakhel-pekudei.notes: Pekudei's haftara (the general rule: when two parshiyos are joined, the second one's haftara is read; Rema on SA OC 428:8). In practice Vayakhel-Pekudei almost always coincides with Parah or HaChodesh, which take precedence (SEF dates sampled show only those). Teimani by the general rule; not separately attested.

tazria-metzora.notes: Metzora's haftara (EnWP; SEF). Teimani by the general rule (Metzora's), not separately attested. Often displaced by Rosh Chodesh Iyar or Shabbos HaGadol.

acharei-mos-kedoshim.notes: Ashkenazim read Acharei Mos's haftara (Amos), an exception to the usual rule of reading the second parsha's haftara (Rema on SA OC 428:8). Sephardim read Kedoshim's (EnWP: S, I Ezekiel 20:2-20). Chabad: CHB 2028-05-06 shows Amos 9:7-15. SEF shows Amos for both customs on most dates, but its Sephardi data is not consistent here. Libya reads Ezekiel 22 when the two are joined (AHT). Teimani not found.

behar-bechukosai.notes: Bechukosai's haftara (EnWP; SEF). Teimani not found (Yemenites read Jeremiah 16:19-17:14 for Behar and Ezekiel 34 for Bechukosai; which one is read when joined is not attested).

chukas-balak.notes: Balak's haftara (EnWP; SEF). Joined only in the Diaspora, when 17 Tammuz falls on a Thursday (EnWP).

matos-masei.notes: Masei's haftara, which is the second haftara of affliction (EnWP; SEF; CHB 2027-07-31). When it falls on Rosh Chodesh Av, see special.shabbos-rosh-chodesh-av. Teimani null, as for masei.

nitzavim-vayelech.notes: Nitzavim's haftara, the seventh of consolation (EnWP; SEF).

shekalim.notes: Shabbos on or before Rosh Chodesh Adar (Adar II in a leap year). Sources: SA OC 685:1 ('Vayichros Yehoyada' = 11:17), EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2028-02-26 / 2025-03-01. Takes precedence over Rosh Chodesh and Machar Chodesh (Rema OC 425:1); see shekalim-rosh-chodesh and shekalim-machar-chodesh.

zachor.notes: Shabbos before Purim. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2028-03-11. Posen ended at 15:33. Teimani 14:52-15:33 per EnWP and HeWP; AHT attributes it to some Yemenites. Also read on Shabbos of Purim Meshulash in Jerusalem (EnWP).

parah.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2028-03-18.

hachodesh.notes: Shabbos on or before Rosh Chodesh Nisan. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2028-03-25 and 2022-04-02 (Chabad 45:18-46:15; EnWP's 'AH 45:18-46:16' is not supported). Frankfurt and Posen Ashkenazim read 45:18-46:15. Takes precedence over Rosh Chodesh and Machar Chodesh; see hachodesh-rosh-chodesh.

shabbos-rosh-chodesh.notes: Read the whole of Isaiah 66, then repeat 66:23. Sources: SA OC 425:1, EnWP, HeWP, AHT, CHB 2027-01-09. SEF gives only 66:1-24 and leaves out the repeated verse. Exceptions (EnWP; SA/Rema OC 425:1; SA OC 684:3, 685): Rosh Chodesh Teves (Chanukah haftara), Adar (Shekalim), Nisan (HaChodesh), Tishrei (Rosh Hashana), Av and Elul (customs differ; see their own keys).

machar-chodesh.notes: Shabbos that is the eve of a Rosh Chodesh that falls on Sunday. Sources: SA OC 425:2, EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-02-06. Not read before Rosh Chodesh Teves (Chanukah), Adar (Shekalim), Nisan (HaChodesh) or Tishrei, and in most communities not before Elul (EnWP). It also does not displace Re'eh's haftara (SA/Rema OC 425:2). Rosh Chodesh Av never falls on Sunday (MB 425:9).

shabbos-rosh-chodesh-and-erev.sephardi: Isaiah 66:1-24; Isaiah 66:23; I Samuel 20:18; I Samuel 20:42
shabbos-rosh-chodesh-and-erev.chabad: Isaiah 66:1-24; Isaiah 66:23; I Samuel 20:18; I Samuel 20:42
shabbos-rosh-chodesh-and-erev.notes: Shabbos that is day 1 of a two-day Rosh Chodesh (the 30th of the month). SA OC 425:2: read Isaiah 66, then add the first and last verse of Machar Chodesh. Rema there (and MB 425:11): do not skip between prophets; read only the Rosh Chodesh haftara, 'and so is the custom'. Chabad follows the addition (SHM: 'Shabbos Rosh Chodesh which is also the eve of Rosh Chodesh'; CHB 2029-08-11). Teimani not found.

shabbos-rosh-chodesh-av.notes: 1 Av on Shabbos (Masei or Matos-Masei). Rema OC 425:1 records both 'Shim'u' (Abudraham, Mordechai) and Isaiah 66 ('and that is primary where there is no custom', Terumas HaDeshen). MB 425:8: the Vilna Gaon rules Shim'u. Most communities read Shim'u (EnWP); some read Isaiah 66 (EnWP; SEF shows Isaiah 66 for 2025-07-26). Chabad reads Shim'u (SHM, citing the Rebbe Rashab) and adds Isaiah 66:1, 66:23-24 and 66:23 (CHB 2025-07-26). Teimani not found.

shabbos-rosh-chodesh-elul.notes: Shabbos Re'eh on Rosh Chodesh Elul. SA OC 425:1: read Re'eh's haftara ('Aniya So'arah') so as not to break up the seven of consolation (Sephardi practice). Rema: some read Isaiah 66, 'and so is the custom in these lands' (Ashkenaz); MB 425:6-7: Isaiah 66 also contains consolation, and the skipped Aniya So'arah is made up on Ki Seitzei. Chabad: Isaiah 66 (SHM; CHB 2029-08-11). If that Shabbos is 30 Av (two-day Rosh Chodesh), Chabad (and SA) also append I Samuel 20:18 and 20:42 (CHB 2029-08-11 shows 'Isaiah 66:1-24; Isaiah 66:23; I Samuel 20:18; I Samuel 20:42'); Ashkenazim per Rema 425:2 do not. Frankfurt read Machar Chodesh when Rosh Chodesh Elul is on Sunday (EnWP). Teimani not found.

machar-chodesh-elul.notes: Shabbos Re'eh on 29 Av, with Rosh Chodesh Elul on Sunday. SA OC 425:2 (gloss): Machar Chodesh does not displace 'Aniya So'arah'. Chabad reads Re'eh's haftara and adds the first and last verse of Machar Chodesh (SHM; CHB 2025-08-23). Some communities, such as Frankfurt, read Machar Chodesh (EnWP). Teimani not found.

ki-seitzei-after-rosh-chodesh-elul.notes: Ki Seitzei in a year when Re'eh's haftara was displaced by Isaiah 66. Ashkenazim read 'Roni Akara' and continue with 'Aniya So'arah' (MB 425:7; EnWP). Chabad does the same (SHM; CHB 2029-08-25). Sephardim read Re'eh's haftara on Re'eh, so nothing needs to be made up.

shekalim-rosh-chodesh.notes: Shekalim on Shabbos Rosh Chodesh Adar: the Shekalim haftara takes precedence (SA OC 685:1; Rema OC 425:1). Chabad adds the first and last verse(s) of Isaiah 66 (CHB 2025-03-01). Dotan (via EnWP) reports that some Sephardim add Isaiah 66:1 and 66:23 to the special haftara on Rosh Chodesh; that is a single secondary source, so it is not encoded. Teimani not found.

shekalim-machar-chodesh.chabad: II Kings 11:17-12:17; I Samuel 20:18; I Samuel 20:42
shekalim-machar-chodesh.notes: Shekalim on Shabbos erev Rosh Chodesh Adar (Rosh Chodesh on Sunday): Shekalim. Chabad adds I Samuel 20:18 and 20:42 (CHB 2028-02-26). Teimani not found.

hachodesh-rosh-chodesh.notes: HaChodesh on Shabbos Rosh Chodesh Nisan: HaChodesh takes precedence (EnWP; Rema OC 425:1). Chabad adds the first and last verse(s) of the Rosh Chodesh haftara (SHM; CHB 2022-04-02), and on erev Rosh Chodesh the first and last verse of Machar Chodesh (SHM; not checked on a CHB page). Dotan (via EnWP): Sephardim and Mizrachim add Isaiah 66:1 and 66:23 (or I Samuel 20:18 and 20:42 on the eve); single source, not encoded. Teimani not found.

shabbos-chanukah-1.notes: Sources: Talmud Megillah 31a, SA OC 684:3, EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-12-05. Displaces the weekly haftara and also Machar Chodesh (EnWP).

shabbos-chanukah-2.notes: Second Shabbos of Chanukah (occurs only when the first day of Chanukah is a Sunday, i.e. the 8th day is Shabbos). Sources: EnWP (A,S,Y,I), HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-12-12.

shabbos-chanukah-rosh-chodesh.notes: Shabbos Chanukah that is Rosh Chodesh Teves: read the Chanukah haftara ('Roni v'simchi', SA OC 684:3; MB 684:11, because publicising the miracle comes first). Chabad adds the first and last verse(s) of Isaiah 66, and when that Shabbos is 30 Kislev (also the eve of the second day of Rosh Chodesh) also I Samuel 20:18 and 20:42: CHB 2022-12-24 and 2015-12-12 show 'Zechariah 2:14-4:7; Isaiah 66:1; Isaiah 66:23-24; Isaiah 66:23; I Samuel 20:18; I Samuel 20:42'. The value encoded here is for a Shabbos that is Rosh Chodesh but not also the eve of Rosh Chodesh. It is inferred from the same Chabad pattern verified for Shekalim (CHB 2025-03-01) and HaChodesh (CHB 2022-04-02) on Rosh Chodesh, but no dated CHB page for that exact case was found. For 30 Kislev, use shabbos-chanukah-rosh-chodesh-and-erev. Teimani not found.

shabbos-chanukah-rosh-chodesh-and-erev.chabad: Zechariah 2:14-4:7; Isaiah 66:1; Isaiah 66:23-24; Isaiah 66:23; I Samuel 20:18; I Samuel 20:42
shabbos-chanukah-rosh-chodesh-and-erev.notes: Shabbos Chanukah on 30 Kislev (day 1 of a two-day Rosh Chodesh Teves). Chanukah haftara (SA OC 684:3). Chabad as printed on CHB 2022-12-24 and 2015-12-12. Teimani not found.

shabbos-hagadol.notes: Customs differ on WHEN it is read (AHT; EnWP; HeWP): (a) every Shabbos HaGadol (many Ashkenazim, Italy, Morocco, Shami Yemenites); (b) only when Erev Pesach falls on Shabbos (Chabad: SHM; SA HaRav 430:3; Belz; Frankfurt at times; confirmed by CHB 2025-04-12 vs 2028-04-08); (c) every year EXCEPT when Erev Pesach is on Shabbos (Vilna Gaon, Ma'aseh Rav; Lithuania); (d) never (Baladi Yemenites, Worms, Izmir). Text: Malachi 3:4-24 with 3:23 repeated (EnWP, HeWP, AHT). CHB's header shows 3:4-24 only. Teimani null: Baladi Yemenites have no special haftara (AHT, HeWP).

shabbos-shuva.notes: Shabbos between Rosh Hashana and Yom Kippur (Vayelech or Haazinu); always 'Shuva' (SA OC 428:8). Ashkenaz: AHT ('common Ashkenazi custom'), HeWP and EnWP (Dotan, Koren, Hirsch, Jerusalem Crown) give Hosea + Joel 2:15-27. Many Ashkenazim (Hertz; Prague, Berlin, Lakewood per AHT; SEF) add both Joel 2:15-27 and Micah 7:18-20, and some start Joel at 2:11. Sephardi: Hosea + Micah (HeWP, EnWP, AHT). Chabad: Hosea + Micah per CHB 2027-10-09 and 2029-09-15, CHB-n (Shabbos Shuva) and HeWP. AHT lists Chabad as adding both Joel and Micah, but the Chabad sources were preferred. Teimani: HeWP, and AHT ('some Yemenites add nothing'); Shami add Micah 7:18-20.

affliction-1.notes: First of the three haftaros of affliction ('Divrei Yirmiyahu'), read on the first Shabbos after 17 Tammuz: Pinchas in most years, Matos when Pinchas falls before 17 Tammuz (SA OC 428:8; EnWP; SEF; CHB 2027-07-24 (Chabad, Pinchas)). Teimani: EnWP and HeWP give 1:1-19; AHT says this is the old Yemenite custom and still that of some Yemenites today.

affliction-2.notes: Second of affliction ('Shim'u'), on Masei or Matos-Masei (SA OC 428:8; EnWP; HeWP; AHT; SEF; CHB 2027-07-31). Week 3 is Devarim (Chazon, Isaiah 1:1-27; see parsha.devarim). On Rosh Chodesh Av see shabbos-rosh-chodesh-av. Teimani null (conflicting; see parsha.masei).

consolation-1.notes: Haftara of vaeschanan (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.vaeschanan for sources.

consolation-2.notes: Haftara of eikev (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.eikev for sources.

consolation-3.notes: Haftara of reeh (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.reeh for sources. If Rosh Chodesh Elul is on this Shabbos, Ashkenazim and Chabad read Isaiah 66 and Sephardim keep this one (shabbos-rosh-chodesh-elul). On erev Rosh Chodesh Elul this one is read, not Machar Chodesh (machar-chodesh-elul).

consolation-4.notes: Haftara of shoftim (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.shoftim for sources.

consolation-5.notes: Haftara of ki-seitzei (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.ki-seitzei for sources. Made up as Isaiah 54:1-55:5 when consolation-3 was displaced (ki-seitzei-after-rosh-chodesh-elul).

consolation-6.notes: Haftara of ki-savo (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.ki-savo for sources.

consolation-7.notes: Haftara of nitzavim (seven of consolation, SA OC 428:8). See parsha.nitzavim for sources. When Nitzavim and Vayelech are joined, this is read.

rosh-hashana-1.notes: Sources: Talmud Megillah 31a (via AHT), AHT (almost all sources), HeWP (I, S, Y), SEF, CHB 2026-09-12. EnWP's 'A, S: 1:1-2:20' conflicts with every other source and is treated as an error.

yom-kippur-shacharis.notes: Sources: EnWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-09-21. HeWP says Sephardim also add 59:20-21. EnWP and AHT give that addition only for Yemenite, Italian and Bukharan Jews; recorded here as a possible Sephardi variant.

yom-kippur-mincha.notes: Sources: Talmud Megillah 31a (via AHT), AHT, OU Haftarah Helper, EnWP, HeWP, CHB-n (Chabad: 'Book of Jonah; Micha 7:18-20'). Frankfurt (and per HeWP some other Ashkenazim) read Jonah without the Micah verses. Italians prefix Obadiah 1:21. Teimani from the generic entries in EnWP and HeWP; no Yemenite variant reported.

sukkos-1.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-09-26.

sukkos-2.notes: Diaspora only. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, CHB 2026-09-27. Teimani null: EnWP gives I Kings 7:51-8:16, HeWP gives 7:51-8:21, and AHT gives 7:51-8:15 (Italy/Yemen) and also 'Yemen: begins at 7:51'. Conflicting.

shabbos-chol-hamoed-sukkos.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2028-10-07.

shemini-atzeres.notes: Diaspora (in Israel the day is Simchas Torah). Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2026-10-03 (Chabad text ends at 8:66). Italians and some Ashkenazim (Mantua) end at 9:1. SHM lists Shemini Atzeres among the haftaros where customs vary, but CHB shows the common range.

simchas-torah.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, CHB 2026-10-04. Some Sephardim append the bridegroom haftara (Isaiah 61:10-62:8); Amsterdam added Isaiah 61:10 and 62:5 (EnWP, AHT).

pesach-1.notes: Ashkenaz: the OU Haftarah Helper gives 3:5-7; 5:2-6:1; 6:27 and calls 3:5-7 optional (read by Chabad and some Ashkenazim). EnWP (Dotan, Benisch) agrees. Other Ashkenazim read only 5:2-6:1 and 6:27; HeWP, SEF and Frankfurt/Perushim read 5:2-6:1 alone. Chabad: CHB 2027-04-22. Sephardi and Teimani: EnWP (generic) and AHT (Sephardim, Yemen, Frankfurt, Berlin). HeWP alone says Sephardim prefix 3:5-7.

pesach-2.notes: Diaspora only. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, OU Haftarah Helper, CHB 2027-04-23. The Vilna Gaon read 23:1-25 except verse 13 (AHT gives 23:1-12, 14-25); some begin at 23:4.

shabbos-chol-hamoed-pesach.notes: Sources: HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-04-24. EnWP gives A, S Ezekiel 37:1-17 (with AH 37:1-14); the majority of sources give 37:1-14. Posen ended at 37:17.

pesach-7.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-04-28.

pesach-8.notes: Diaspora only. Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT, SEF, CHB 2027-04-29.

shavuos-2.notes: Diaspora only. Sources: OU Haftarah Helper (2:20-3:19), EnWP (generic), HeWP (S, I), CHB 2027-06-12. Many Ashkenazim recite Yetziv Pisgam after the first verse (2:20). HeWP, SEF and AHT ('most Ashkenazi chumashim') begin at 3:1, i.e. Habakkuk 3:1-19. Teimani not found.

tisha-bav-shacharis.notes: Sources: Talmud Megillah 31b (via AHT), EnWP, HeWP, AHT.

tisha-bav-mincha.notes: Sources: EnWP, HeWP, AHT. Teimani null: EnWP gives Hosea 14:2-10 and Micah 7:18-20, while HeWP and AHT (Baladi) give Hosea 14:2-10 alone.

fast-day-mincha.notes: 'Dirshu'; Ashkenaz minchah on public fasts other than Tisha B'Av, including Tzom Gedaliah (SA OC 428:8; Rema OC 566:1 via AHT; EnWP; HeWP; AHT). Sephardi null because most Sephardi communities read no haftara at minchah of a fast day (EnWP; HeWP). Some, mainly in Morocco and Algeria, read Dirshu (Isaiah 55:6-56:8), and a few read Hosea 14:2-10 with Micah 7:18-20 (AHT; EnWP via Dotan). Teimani: no haftara (EnWP; HeWP), so null.
